$comment: What the provenance marks claim, and what may be left unmarked.
`forkAdded` is DERIVED, not authored: it is keys(local) - keys(master),
and check-fork-marks.mjs recomputes it from git and fails when this file
disagrees in either direction. Edit it only to record what that check has
already told you. It is written down at all so a rebase that brings a key
upstream produces a visible diff rather than a silently changed answer.
`configOnly` is the opposite: it CANNOT be computed. The sweep that looks
for keys with no control is wrong in both directions — see `excluded` —
so every entry here was confirmed by hand and carries its reason.
The runtime never reads this file. The marks live in the templates; this
exists to be the thing they are held against.
switchRows: Mark the settings this fork added

configOnly.why: Read three times in tabby-core/src/services/app.service.ts to decide whether next/previous tab wraps around. Upstream ships it with no control anywhere; this fork gives it one on the Window page.

Read in tabby-terminal/src/api/baseTerminalTab.component.ts, where a percentage in the output drives the tab's progress bar and the taskbar icon. Upstream ships it with no control; this fork gives it one on the Terminal page.

configOnlyUnexposed.why: A real upstream setting: app/lib/app.ts registers it with globalShortcut. No control anywhere, and not exposed here either - a hotkey spec string needs a picker, not a text box. Recorded so the sweep does not ask again, not because it is settled.

A real upstream setting: tabby-local/src/session.ts merges it into every session environment. No control anywhere, and not exposed here - a key/value editor is a bigger piece of UI than this change is about.

notSettings.why: Not a setting. It is where the search panel persists the state of its own toggles (searchPanel.component.ts writes regex/caseSensitive back into it), so it correctly has no settings row.
Declared in upstream's defaults and referenced by no TypeScript in the tree. Dead upstream, so there is nothing to expose and nothing to mark.
An unfinished upstream rename: configDefaults.yaml declares electronFlags while app/lib/app.ts reads configStore.flags. The default is dead either way.
Declared in upstream's defaults and referenced nowhere in the tree.

knownGaps.why: Declared under platformDefaults (Windows), which the checker does not parse because its keys are computed - [Platform.Windows] would come out as a nonsense path. Fork-added, and has no settings row either way.

excluded.why: Edited generically by the Hotkeys page from the HotkeyProviders, never by key, so no row ever names one.
Edited through editProfileModal and the per-type profile settings components, which bind to profile.options.* rather than to config.store.
As profiles: edited through the profile tree, never as a config path.
Machinery, not a setting: the encrypted store's own contents.
The config schema version, migrated by upstream's own code.
Edited by the Config sync page through its own service rather than by binding to the keys.

Has a full editor, reached as config.store.terminal[this.configKey] with the key passed in as a template input (colorSchemeSettingsForMode.component.ts) — so its name appears as a literal nowhere. The trap this sweep cannot see through.
Edited by the Color scheme page through its own service.
Edited by the Plugins page through the plugin manager, not by a settings row.
Written by the app itself when saving the tab layout, not chosen by anyone.
Only meaningful in the web build, which has its own settings surface.
Edited through the SSH profile settings components against profile.options.*.
